skill.name: shodan-reconnaissance
skill.description: Guides authorized Shodan reconnaissance using CLI, web, API, filters, exports, monitoring, and reporting for exposed internet assets.
skill.summary: Authorized workflows for discovering and documenting exposed services with Shodan.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most Ruby backtick, API-key, hardcoded-IP, and certificate findings are documentation false positives because they are Markdown examples or placeholders. Confirmed issues include the elevated installation command, Shodan API network calls, and reconnaissance workflows for active scanning and exposed vulnerable services. No prompt injection attempt was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.suggestion: Replace sudo package-manager installation with non-privileged install guidance or require explicit user approval before any elevated command.

remediation.issue: Active scanning and vulnerable target discovery
remediation.suggestion: Add a mandatory authorization check, scope confirmation, and refusal guidance for arbitrary third-party targets before scan or vulnerability-search workflows.
Use environment variables or a secure secret prompt instead of inline API key placeholders in commands and scripts.
Add data minimization, redaction, and storage guidance for downloaded Shodan results and screenshots.

content.value_statement: Exposed internet assets create risk when teams cannot see them. This skill provides Shodan workflows for authorized searches, filters, exports, and reports.
actual_capabilities: Install and initialize the Shodan command-line tool.
Query single hosts, domains, organizations, ports, products, and CVEs.
Download, parse, and export Shodan result sets for analysis.
Submit and monitor Shodan on-demand scans for authorized targets.
Use Shodan REST API and Python library examples.
Explain Shodan credits, data freshness, and legal boundaries.
limitations: Requires a Shodan account and user-supplied API key.
Some searches, downloads, scans, and historical data require paid credits.
Shodan data can be stale and needs validation before reporting.
Does not verify exploitability or authorize testing against third parties.

use_cases.title: External Exposure Review
use_cases.description: Find public services for owned domains and networks before publishing an exposure report.

use_cases.title: Pentest Reconnaissance Prep
use_cases.description: Build an authorized target inventory with ports, products, versions, and likely vulnerabilities.

use_cases.title: Incident Scoping
use_cases.description: Search Shodan for exposed indicators, affected services, and public infrastructure during response.

prompt_templates.title: Check One Host
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to plan a Shodan lookup for this authorized IP address: [IP]. Summarize expected fields and safe next steps.

prompt_templates.title: Inventory Owned Domain
prompt_templates.prompt: Create Shodan queries for the owned domain [DOMAIN]. Include hostname, organization, product, and port filters with reporting notes.

prompt_templates.title: Review Vulnerable Services
prompt_templates.prompt: Given these authorized targets [SCOPE], design Shodan searches for exposed vulnerable services and explain validation limits.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Reconnaissance Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a full Shodan reconnaissance workflow for [CLIENT SCOPE]. Include authorization checks, credit use, exports, evidence handling, and final deliverables.

output_examples.input: Find exposed services for an owned example.com domain.
output_examples.output: A concise asset inventory with hostnames, IP addresses, observed ports, products, versions, and validation steps.

output_examples.input: Summarize Shodan results for an authorized cloud IP range.
output: Exposure summary grouped by service and region.
Likely stale records separated from current scan candidates.
Recommended owner validation and remediation priorities.

output_examples.input: Prepare a report from downloaded Shodan data.
output_examples.output: A human-readable report outline with findings, affected assets, evidence notes, limitations, and authorized follow-up actions.

best_practices: Use only targets where you have written authorization.
Store Shodan API keys outside prompts and shared files.
Record query dates, filters, credits, and data freshness in reports.
anti_patterns: Searching random vulnerable devices without permission.
Treating stale Shodan data as proof without validation.
Publishing raw banners, screenshots, or host lists that expose third parties.

faq.question: Does this skill run Shodan automatically?
faq.answer: It provides workflows and command examples. Any real query or scan still requires user action and valid credentials.

faq.question: Is this only for paid Shodan accounts?
faq.answer: No. Basic lookups can work on free accounts, but filtered searches, exports, scans, and history may need credits.

faq.question: Can it prove that a system is vulnerable?
faq.answer: No. Shodan data is an indicator. Confirm findings with authorized validation and current asset owner records.

faq.question: How should API keys be handled?
faq.answer: Use secure local configuration, environment variables, or secret storage. Do not paste real keys into shared prompts or files.

faq.question: Can it scan any public IP range?
faq.answer: No. Active scans and targeted reconnaissance should be limited to networks where you have explicit authorization.

faq.question: What output should teams expect?
faq.answer: Typical output includes asset inventories, service summaries, CVE indicators, export plans, and report-ready limitations.
